{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --time=00:30:00
#   --mem=24G
#   --gpus=1
#   --nodes=1

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --time-limit=30m

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=24G
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --gpus=1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/tysweat0/.conda/envs/img2img/lib/python3.9/site-packages/nvidia/cublas/lib

cd "$HOME/StableComics/FullPipeline/"

nvidia-smi --list-gpus
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total --format=csv

python run.py
"
}

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 GPU (`--gpus=1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job requested 24G of memory (`--mem=24G`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this may under-provision the job and risk OOM.
